utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Good afternoon, everybody. Good afternoon to the Prosecution, to the Defence, to Mr. Djordjevic. Mr. Registrar, would you be so kind as to announce the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case IT-05-87/1-PT, The Prosecutor versus Vlastimir Djordjevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We are here this afternoon in the occasion of the amendment to the indictment which was granted by the Chamber on I think 7th July, and the purpose of this hearing is to ask you, Mr. Djordjevic, to enter a plea of guilty or not guilty today to the new count that has been included in the indictment as a result of the Trial Chamber's decision. So we are here under Rule 50(b) to allow you to enter your plea; and as you may recall, the Prosecution moved for amendment of the indictment to include a new charge of murder in Podujevo and also to include not new charges but inclusion of new victims relating to two charges that had already been included in the indictment, namely the incidents that took place in Suva Reka and in Vucitrn. And on 9th July pursuant to the Chambers order, the Prosecution filed the new indictment. The indictment alleges that you, Mr. Djordjevic, took part in a joint criminal enterprise to modify the ethnic balance in Kosovo in order to ensure the continued Serbian control in the area. The indictment further alleges that the purpose of the joint criminal enterprise was to be achieved through a widespread or systematic campaign of terror or violence including the crimes charged in the indictment. A number of individuals formed part of this joint criminal enterprise together with you, including Milan Milutinovic, Nikola Sainovic, Dragoljub Ojdanic, Nebojsa Pavkovic, Vladimir Lazarevic, and Sreten Lukic. Counts 3 and 4 of the indictment allege killings of hundreds of Kosovo Albanian men, women, and children throughout the province of Kosovo. The killings were allegedly committed between 1st January and 20th of June, 1999, by the forces of federal -- the Republic of Yugoslavia and the Republic of Yugoslavia in whose service you took part. The incidents of mass killings which the Prosecution charges under count 3 and 4 are listed in paragraph 75 of the indictment. As a result of the added new charge, paragraph 75(l) now includes the Podujevo incident. Furthermore, in relation to the Suva Reka incident charged in paragraph 75(d), as Delta, the Prosecution was granted leave to add the names of three further victims to Schedule (d), as Delta; and also in relation to the Vucitrn incident charged in paragraph 75(i), for India, the prosecution was granted leave to add the name of one further victim to Schedule (i). Mr. Djordjevic - I'm addressing counsel Djordjevic now - has the accused received a copy of the amended indictment?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, as Defence counsel for the accused Vlastimir Djordjevic, I have to say that he was served a copy of the indictment in a language he understands only late in the evening, and in fact, due to procedural reasons, this fact could have been registered in the appropriate protocol only early this morning. I consider this in a way to be a violation of the accused person's right to Defence. However, since the counts from the third amended indictment resemble to a great degree the fourth amended indictment, and also there is the fact that we were allowed as a special circumstance a visit this afternoon lasting one hour. We talked to our client, and we thought that it was in our interest to allow him to enter his plea this afternoon, although, it is impermissible to have this kind of thing happen, namely to have a copy of the indictment served on him in a language he understands. We decided nevertheless that he does enter a plea because it is in our interest, and he is going to do that today with regard to the new counts in the indictment and the incidents described by the OTP in the fourth amended indictment against accused Vlastimir Djordjevic. Once again I express my regret on account of what had happened, and I believe that it is truly not proper to receive early in the morning such serious charges against yourself, and then within a few hours without looking into the other circumstances you have the possibility of entering your plea. He is going to do that today, nevertheless, observing Rule 50(c), I believe, of the rules of procedure and evidence, and we are going to be in a position to file some preliminary motions within the next 30 days. So, Your Honour, I would like to inform you of the fact that our client will enter a plea today. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you for this information, counsel, and I regret on behalf of the Tribunal the delay that has occurred here in relation to the service of the amended indictments on your client. I take it, however, that you and your client were given a copy of the motion earlier on and that at least the English version of the amended indictment did reach you in time, so I hope that we are not seriously damaging the justice of your client.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, once again I wish to point out that that is precisely the reason why we are going to enter our plea today in view of the amended indictment. Formally, we know how things stand, and we know that the accused has to be served a copy of the indictment in his own language. Why this was not done, I don't know, but I cannot -- but not mention it today for the simple reason that this kind of thing should not happen again. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I fully agree with you, and as I said, I apologise on behalf of the Tribunal, and I am grateful for your flexibility and openness. Mr. Djordjevic, would you please stand up. Under the statute and the rules, you enjoy the right to remain silent at all times if you wish, but I understand from what your counsel has just said that you are willing to enter your plea today. Let me just for the sake of clarity read out the addition that has been made to the indictment in respect of the Podujevo incidents, and that reads as follows, it's very short: "On or about the 28th March of 1999, forces of the former Republic of Yugoslavia and Serbia killed at least 14 members of the Bogujevci, Duriqi, and Llugaliu families, all women and children, in the courtyard of a house in the town of Podujevo. A group of 19 women and children were ordered to gather in the courtyard, and 14 were killed and 5 children were seriously injured in the shooting. Those persons killed are known by name and set forth in Schedule L, which is attached as an appendix to this indictment." This is the inclusion that has been made, and I wish to ask you, Mr. Djordjevic, if you plead guilty or not guilty to this new charge.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you very much we will enter your pleading of not guilty in the record. You may sit. I just want to be sure that in addition to this new charge, that the Defence is also aware and the accused, of course, is aware of the inclusion of three new victims in the Suva Reka incident and one new victim in the Vucitrn incident. Can you affirm this?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we are fully aware of the indictment, and we confirm that we are aware of the way in which the OTP amended the indictment by including new charges. As I said, we are going to use legal recourse that is available to us in view of our client's plea within the next 30 days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You mentioned awhile ago, counsel, that you intend to file a preliminary motion under Rule 72; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just said that I retain the right to do that after more extensive consultations that we are going to have tomorrow during the work meeting that we are going to have at the UNDU. That will certainly last for three hours, and after that we are definitely going to decide whether we are going to file a preliminary motion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you. May I just remind you that in that case, the 30-day limit will start on the 9th of July -- the 7th of July, sorry, on the day of the decision. This brings us to the end of the formal part of this hearing, and I would then like to raise another matter, which relates to a motion that I have received from the Prosecution asking for extension of time in relation to the extra investigations that had to be made after the testimony of General Aleksandar Dimitrijevic in the Milutinovic trial. I understand that the Prosecution is asking for two more weeks to submit their pre-trial brief, and I realise by now that I did not ask for the presentation of the parties in today's hearing, so I would like you to introduce yourself, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. It's Priya Gopalan and myself, Chester Stamp, for the Prosecution. With us is our case manager, Mr. Colin Nawrot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Welcome to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: As you are aware, we have issued a scheduling order to request the Prosecution to file its pre-trial brief on Monday the 25th of August, and the Defence to file its pretrial brief on Monday, the 15th of September. Since I know that the Defence has asked for more time to prepare its case, and since I know that, also, the Prosecution had requested an extension of time at the last status conference, we had a discussion about this, and I indicated the Chamber's firm commitment to have the case made ready for start -- the trial made ready for start by mid-October. This stands unchanged. I am not sure that the reason the Prosecution has put forward as in support of its motion for extension of time is really convincing. The fact that you have had a two-day testimony of General Dimitrijevic Milutinovic would not seem to me to be a factor that requires an extension of two week's time to submit your pretrial brief. So at least from a starting point, I'm not inclined to grant your motion. However, as you can recall from our discussions here when we had the last -- at the last status conference, we did include one extra week because we anticipated that there could arise unforeseen circumstances. So we do in fact have one week to give to the -- to each of the parties. And since I believe that the reasons put forward by the Prosecution for extension of time does not warrant a delay of two weeks, then on the other hand since we do have an extra week at our disposal, I'm determined to grant the Prosecution's motion in the sense that we will delay the filing of the pre-trial briefs with this extra week. That is to say, my proposal is that we change or we alter the scheduling order so as to now set the time limit for submission of the Prosecution's pretrial brief for Monday, the 1st of September, and equally to move down one week for the Defence from the 15th of September to the 22nd of September. This will still allow us to start the trial in mid-October as scheduled or as planned, at least. Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: If the Chamber will give you this extra week, will you then promise me that there will be no more requests for delays?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: On the basis of what I know now, I make that promise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Because I must say that -- I must be frank with you that whatever comes up from now on will not be granted. There will be no more delays than this one. We had this extra week because we thought that there might come up something. Now something has arisen. I don't know if the grounds are sufficient, but since we do have this week, I'm prepared to go along with your requests and grant it. But that's the end, and there will be no more delays.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Please respect this and take it into account, and this goes, as well, for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: We will do all that is necessary to comply with the deadlines, and we'll do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: So it is hereby decided, and the scheduling order will follow in writing, that the Prosecution is now to submit its pretrial brief on Monday, the 1st of September, and the Defence will file its pretrial brief on Monday, the 22nd of September. Mr. Djordjevic, do you have anything to add?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. First of all, I wanted to say that the Defence has accepted the scheduling order given previously, bearing in mind that from the 15th of September, which was our last deadline for the pre-trial brief submission, until the envisaged beginning of the trial, we had more of a time lapse than we are going to have now. So I still don't have the scheduling order indicating when the trial against the accused Djordjevic would begin. However, if it is indeed the date that you have just given us, the 13th of October, then given the extension of the deadline for the Prosecution and for the Defence, as well, that means that from that date until the beginning of the trial, which is the 13th of October, we have literally a week less than we had under the previous deadline. So based on some earlier plans that we have, the Defence would normally agree to this extension of deadline providing that the beginning of the trial is also postponed by a week because that would be in compliance with the plan based on which the Defence has been working until now. Otherwise, our plan so far would be effected. However, we will always abide by whatever the Chamber says. There are some additional problems there. I don't want to repeat myself. I have stated those problems earlier, and I will admit that we are in somewhat better position than our colleagues who were Defence lawyers in the Milutinovic case. But on the other hand, we have some other circumstances that represent a burden to us because when we start the trial, there will still not be any judgement in the Milutinovic case, so we have to take that into account when working on this case. That's all I have to say. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Djordjevic. May I just note that the time you have from now on until the trial starts remains unchanged. The only thing that has changed is that you are being offered an opportunity to submit your pre-trial brief a week later than originally anticipated, and may I repeat that I'm not in a position to confirm that the trial will start on Monday, the 13th of October. My indication has been that it will start in mid-October. I assume that this will be sometime during that week that starts with Monday, the 13th of October, but whether it's going to be Monday or Tuesday or Wednesday, I can't say because this will be in the end for the Trial Chamber to determine exactly when it wishes to have the pre-trial conference and the opening statements. It may be Monday the 13th, but it may also be at some later date. I will leave that, respectfully, to the Trial Chamber to determine for itself. What I can do is that I can ensure that the trial is made ready to begin by mid-October, and this is my promise to the President, and I do so by asking the parties to file their pre-trial briefs on the dates that we have now agreed upon. So that's all I have to say regarding this matter. Mr. Djordjevic, are you still in good shape?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I am in pretty good shape. I'm a bit concerned due to this great haste which exists in my case. Today, it's exactly one year and one month that I have been here, so I think that there's plenty of time to put me on trial. However, I believe that this Court will take into consideration all facts, and then this excessive haste will not effect my case. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Djordjevic. Maybe I should say that the fact that you have been here already for one year is in itself, in my view, too long, so I think it's about high time we get on with your trial. And as we have said at the last status conference and at many previous status conferences before the last, the fact that the judgement in Milutinovic will not be rendered until later cannot remain a factor that should delay your trial. When the judgement is actually rendered in Milutinovic, and we don't know the dates as of yet, then I'm sure that the parties will have an opportunity to adjust their strategies in light of what is decided in the Milutinovic judgement; but as I said last time, let's cross that bridge when we get there. I think the important thing is to get your trial started, and if the judgement in Milutinovic calls for any amendments, I think it's for the Trial Chamber to deal with that at that time. But I'm glad that you can confirm that you are still in good health, and may I ask you if you have any other issues that you wish to raise at this occasion, since we are here together now?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, there are some other issues concerning my financial situation and facts to establish that. They are treating me as though I were Rockefeller, and it is my impression that there is some kind of special procedure instituted against me. I guess that this will be the fastest case before this Court. There are some cases where people waited for a trial for three or five years, and my trial is to begin after one year, and I am interested in having a speedy trial, but I hope that this excessive haste will not affect the issues of my responsibility or any issues concerning my defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I can assure you, Mr. Djordjevic, that you will be given a fair trial that lives up to the same standards as any other accused before this Tribunal. There is no difference made between you and anybody else, and as I've said before, I think the fact that some of your co- -- some of the other accused before us have had to wait for several years before their trial could start is, in my view, something that is only deplorable. It has to do with organisational problems and other sorts of issues, but it is really deplorable that people would have to wait for so long before their trial could start after they have been arrested. No more to be said about this. I wish to ask the parties if they have any other issue to raise at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Nothing, Your Honour. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Nothing for the time being, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: As regards the financial issue that your client raised, I will instruct my senior legal officer to contact you and to see if there are any problems that can be sorted out in this respect. This concludes the second or the third initial appearance as it is, and we stand adjourned. Thank you.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2:53 p.m.
